test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A trader lost 5% by selling a shirt for ₹950. He will gain x% by selling it for ₹1,360. The value of x is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 5% means the **Selling Price (SP₁)** is 95% of the **Cost Price (CP)**.

Given SP₁ = 950 ⇒ 95% of CP = 950 ⇒ 1% of CP = 10.

The new Selling Price (SP₂) = 1360.

As 10 corresponds to 1%, 1360 corresponds to (1360 ÷ 10) = 136%.

New Profit % (x) = 136% − 100% = 36%.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = 950, Loss₁% = 5%, SP₂ = 1360.

**Formulas:** CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%], Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96e48d298d57580aa86be0bd611d1151bf242c36cfa03be084cf7a35b5278bc4.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Find **Cost Price (CP)** = [950 × 100] ÷ [100 − 5] = [950 × 100] ÷ 95 = 1000.

⇒ Step 2: New **Profit** = SP₂ − CP = 1360 − 1000 = 360.

⇒ Step 3: **x%** = (360 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 36%.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price & Selling Price Relationship

When there is a profit, SP = CP × (100 + P%)/100. When there is a loss, SP = CP × (100 − L%)/100.

Profit Percentage

Profit % is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless otherwise specified in the problem.</p
